descriptor.scene: The frame is the sky itself: high above the jungle canopy, which reads as a soft green sea along the bottom of the frame, THREE small pale-wood crates drift down under small round cream parachutes of plain cloth, at different depths and heights, cords taut, the farthest a tiny speck against warm morning cloud. In the lower left, one canopy gap opens to the forest floor, where a fourth crate has already landed and sits pried open in the ferns exactly as the compass's crated reference paints it: straw packing, and inside, the orange compass reading as one bright coin of clay orange, its short braided cream cord spilling over the crate's edge. NO lettering, stencil or logo on any crate, chute or the compass face. Composition: parachutes stepped across the upper right and middle sky, the opened crate small in the lower left gap; the bottom-right region stays soft canopy for the caption.
negatives: people or figures anywhere in this image
lettering, stencils, numbers or logos on any crate, parachute or compass
an antique compass-rose, star, tick marks, letters or numbers on any compass face (each face is plain cream with ONE dark orange-tipped needle only)
brass-only or gold-only compass shells (every compass shell is burnt-clay ORANGE enamel with only a thin brass rim)
military, cargo or supply-drop vocabulary (no pallets, no netting, no aircraft in frame)
descriptor._caption: The founders up top tell stories too, and send them down. The pages fall a long way, and they land smudged into advice that points at nothing. So the island's keepers send something surer. Small crates drift down under parachutes, and inside each one is a smart orange compass whose needle always swings toward the live portal. The keepers want as many through as they can get. Rumor says the ones holding a sky-compass find the portal long before anyone else.
